title: Interior cleaning and treatment
audience: Car detailers who clean and treat vehicle interiors, including fabric, leather, vinyl and plastic trim.
learningOutcomes: Sequence an interior clean from loose debris to protection, in the order the guides describe.
Select a cleaner and a protectant for fabric, leather, vinyl and plastic from each product's label and SDS.
Keep liquids off screens, controls and electrical parts, and leave the interior dry at handover.

instruction.heading: Order of work
instruction.body: Interior work follows a fixed order, because each step makes the next one easier. Start by removing the mats carefully so debris does not fall onto the carpet, and shake them outside the vehicle. Clear loose items, then vacuum and brush from the top of the cabin downward, so dust falls onto areas you have yet to clean. The Spanish-language manual describes this top-to-bottom sweep for the same reason. Use a firm bristle brush to loosen debris embedded in carpet, working from the outside of each area towards a central pile, and then vacuum the pile. Small brushes and detail tools reach the gaps around door panels and air vents. Spot treat stains only after the loose soil is out, because a cleaner applied over grit smears the grit into the fibres. An extraction machine can deepen the clean on fabric. The Spanish manual calls it expensive and optional, and this lesson treats it the same way.

instruction.heading: Matching the product to the material
instruction.body: Each material needs its own approach. Fabric and carpet take a cleaner suited to the fibre, applied to a brush or applicator, worked in, left for the dwell time on the label, and lifted with a clean towel or the vacuum. The Auto-Detailing guide's dwell example of one to two minutes is an example only, so the label governs. Leather is cleaned and conditioned, and the guide's example applies a conditioner first and a separate cleaner second, with both removed afterwards. Whatever the sequence, the finish should be neither greasy nor glossy, and the guide advises against products that add shine. Do not use heat as a shortcut. The guide describes a hair dryer or heated seats to open the leather, and that method is not adopted here, because heat inside a closed cabin needs its own risk assessment. Vinyl, plastic and rubber take a cleaner followed by a protectant. The Spanish manual warns against spraying dressing directly onto plastic, because it can leave marks, so apply it to an applicator, wipe it on, and buff off the excess with a clean dry towel.

instruction.heading: Protection and finishing
instruction.body: Protect fabric only when it is completely dry, because a protectant sealed onto damp fabric traps moisture. The guides describe a light mist from the product's label, which leaves the fabric feeling natural while adding resistance to moisture and stains. Treat trim with a protectant that gives UV protection and a non-greasy finish, and wipe off any excess so nothing pools on surfaces a driver touches. Keep microfibre in groups, wash it only with other microfibre, and avoid fabric softener, because softener coats the fibres and reduces absorbency and cleaning power. Interior glass needs little cleaner and several towels to avoid streaks. The Auto-Detailing guide notes that the top edge of the glass and the window seal are often missed, so roll the window down a little to reach them.

instruction.heading: Electronics, moisture and handover
instruction.body: Screens, instrument clusters, switches and airbag covers are not places for liquid. Spray product onto an applicator or towel rather than onto the surface, and wipe screens with a dry microfibre towel. Do not disturb airbag covers or exposed wiring. If you find loose trim or an exposed wire, record it, stop work on that item, and refer it to a qualified repairer. Keep carpets as dry as possible, because a wet carpet can hold moisture against the floor for longer than the owner expects. Check the seats and carpets for damp patches before handover, and record anything still wet. Some interior products release vapour in a closed cabin, so ventilation and the cabin risk described in “Cabin air and vapour exposure” apply.

procedure: Remove the mats and shake debris outside the vehicle.
Clear loose items, then vacuum and brush from the top of the cabin downward.
Identify each interior material and select the cleaner the label lists for it.
Apply cleaner to a brush or applicator, work it in, and respect the label's dwell time.
Lift residue with a clean towel and vacuum any loosened debris.
Apply protectant only to a dry surface named on its label, and wipe off the excess.
Dry the interior, check for damp areas, and record the result.

workedExamples.situation: A family SUV has dried juice on a cloth seat, crumbs in the carpet, and a cracked dashboard top with a faded finish.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the order of work, and what do you record about the cracked dashboard?
workedExamples.reasoning: Remove the mats, clear the loose items, vacuum and brush the carpet and seat. Spot treat the juice with a fabric cleaner for the label's dwell time, lift it with a clean towel, and check it is dry. Apply the protectant to the dry trim, but not as a repair to the cracked area. Record the crack as found with a photograph, and state that repair is outside the detailing scope.

workedExamples.situation: A leather seat has a greasy film from an earlier dressing. The owner asks for a glossy finish to match the dashboard.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you tell the owner, and what do you apply?
workedExamples.reasoning: Explain that a glossy or greasy finish is not suited to leather, and that it can attract dirt and wear the surface. Test a leather cleaner on a small area first, then clean the seat for the label's dwell time. Condition the leather as the label directs, and aim for a finish that is neither glossy nor greasy. Record the test result and the finish the owner agreed to.

equipmentAndPpe: Vacuum with brush and crevice tools.
Firm bristle brush, soft and medium brushes, and small detail brushes.
Applicators for each material, and microfibre towels in labelled groups.
Labelled spray bottles for diluted products, mixed as the label directs.
PPE: gloves and eye protection when handling concentrates, as the SDS requires. Ventilate the cabin when using solvent-containing products (SDS flash point).

commonErrors.error: Spraying product directly onto the dashboard or a screen.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply product to an applicator and wipe it on. Keep product off screens and controls.

commonErrors.error: Applying a glossy dressing to leather or the steering wheel.
commonErrors.prevention: Choose a non-greasy finish and test it first.
Vacuum and brush first, then clean.
Work to the label's dwell time, then lift the residue.
Dry the fabric before protecting it.

commonErrors.error: Washing microfibre with other fabrics or with softener.
commonErrors.prevention: Wash microfibre only with microfibre, with no softener.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Interior products have labels and SDSs. Where an SDS names gloves or ventilation, use them. Solvent-containing products need ventilation; see “Cabin air and vapour exposure” for cabin vapour exposure.

Work on airbag covers, exposed wiring or electrical systems is outside detailing and needs a qualified repairer. This lesson does not grant any authority or licence to carry out electrical or airbag work.

qualityStandard: Each material is cleaned with a product its label lists for that material.
No liquid is sprayed onto screens, controls or airbag covers.
The interior is dry at handover, and any damp area is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Interior material and product record, with the label or SDS reference for each product.
Record of any loose trim, crack or exposed wire found, with a photograph and the referral.
summary: Clear and vacuum before any cleaning, and work from top to bottom.
Match the cleaner and the protectant to each material, and follow the label.
Keep liquid off screens and controls, and hand over a dry interior.

knowledgeChecks.question: A seat is wet from a spill. What should happen before a protectant is applied?
options: Apply the protectant at once to seal the spill before it can soak in deeper
Dry the seat completely, then apply the protectant to the surface named on its label
Apply a heavy coat to the wet area so it bonds with the damp fabric quickly
Use a hair dryer on high heat so the seat is dry quickly before the next step

knowledgeChecks.question: Which finish is correct for leather?
options: A glossy finish that repels dirt
A greasy finish that lasts longer
A finish that matches the dashboard

knowledgeChecks.question: A screen is dirty. What is the correct method?
options: Spray cleaner straight onto the screen and wipe it off with a paper towel to finish
Apply product to a towel and wipe with a dry microfibre towel, keeping liquid off the screen
Wet the screen with water and leave it to dry before the next step begins in the car
Use the dashboard dressing on the screen to give it a clean and shiny finish at the end
